title: Preclinical testing of chimeric antigen receptor T cells in neuroblastoma mouse models
protocol: Seed IMR5-5-luc-eGFP cells at low passages (4–10) in T175 flasks at approximately 30% confluency in RPMI-1640 complete medium.
Trypsinize and collect cells when they reach 80%-90% confluency.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min at 300 × g.
Resuspend cell pellet at a density of 2.5 × 10^7/mL in PBS.
Filter resuspended cells through a 40 μm cell strainer before counting.
Keep cells on ice until inoculation.
Inject NSG female mice, aged 5-7 weeks, with 0.2 ml of the cell suspension (5.0 × 10^6 cells) into the tail vein.
Inject D-luciferin solution (15 mg/mL) into the peritoneal cavity of each mouse.
Place the mice inside an anesthetic induction chamber.
Sedate the mice with isoflurane gas at a concentration of 2.5% and a flow rate of 2 L/min for approximately 2-3 minutes.
Inject D-luciferin into the mice ten minutes before imaging.
Transfer the anesthetized mice to the IVIS imaging chamber.
Acquire images for 1 minute.
Record the total photon flux in the region of interest to monitor tumor growth.
Prepare a single-cell suspension of IMR-5 cells at a concentration of 0.25 × 10^6/mL for injection per mouse, including an excess of 20%.
Resuspend the prepared cells in ice-cold Matrigel matrix equaling 30 μL per injection and keep on ice.
Shave the left flank of 5 to 7-week-old female NSG mice to expose a 1 cm × 1 cm area overlaying the spleen.
Place mice under anesthesia with isoflurane and position them in a lateral right recumbent position.
Make a 1.0 cm transverse cutaneous incision at the height of the spleen.
Carefully dissect down to penetrate the peritoneum.
Lift the spleen cranially to visualize the left adrenal gland.
Using a 29-gauge non-hub needle, inject 30 μL of the tumor cell suspension into the periadrenal fat pad.
Close the peritoneum with vicryl sutures.
Close the skin with clips.
Inject 30 μL buprenorphine extended-release subcutaneously for analgesia.
Inject 0.5 mL of 0.9% normal saline subcutaneously for supportive care.
Monitor post-operative animals for pain, bleeding, or other complications.
Remove clips 14 days after surgery if institutional requirements allow.
Inject 0.2 mL of the 15 mg/mL D-luciferin solution into each mouse to detect tumor growth.
Place the mice inside an anesthetic induction chamber.
Sedate the mice with isoflurane gas (2.5% at a flow rate of 2 L/min) approximately 2-3 minutes after D-luciferin injection.
Place the sedated mice into the IVIS imaging chamber.
Acquire images five minutes after D-luciferin injection for a total acquisition time of 60 seconds.
Determine the total photon flux in the region of interest to monitor tumor growth.
Randomize and group mice for CAR T cell treatment based on their bioluminescence signal strength.
Seed Lenti-X™ 293T cells at low passages (4–10) at a density of 20 × 106 cells per Poly-D-lysine–coated 15 cm dish.
Transfect Lenti-X™ 293T cells with the CT3 CAR plasmid, envelope, and packaging plasmids at a ratio of 4:1:3 using lipofectamine 2000 as the transfection reagent.
Replace medium with fresh DMEM complete medium 6–12 hours after transfection.
Harvest the lentivirus-containing supernatants 48–72 hours post-transfection.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes and then filter through a sterile 0.45 μm filter.
Combine 1 volume of Lenti-XTM Concentrator with 3 volumes of clarified supernatant.
Incubate mixture at 4°C for 30 minutes to overnight (12–24 hours).
Centrifuge sample at 1,500 × g for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in 1/20th to 1/100th of the original volume using AIM-V complete medium.
Immediately titrate lentivirus or store at -80°C in single-use aliquots.
Seed Lenti-X™ 293T cells at a density of 1×10^5 cells in a 12-well cell culture plate.
Remove medium from the well designated for counting and count cells; they should be between 1–3 × 10^5 cells/well.
Prepare dilutions of concentrated lentivirus as shown in Figure 4.
Transduce one well with 1 μL, another with 10^-1 μL, and a third with 10^-2 μL of lentivirus in 1 mL of fresh DMEM complete medium.
Keep an additional well as non-transduced control.
After 48–72 hours of transduction, trypsinize cells and collect them in microcentrifuge tubes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in FACS buffer containing 1 μg/mL cetuximab.
Non-infected cells also need to be stained with cetuximab as Lenti-X™ 293T cells express hEGFRt.
Keep cells at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 20 min.
Wash cells once with PBS.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer containing the RPE F(ab’)2 goat anti-human IgG antibody at a 1:200 dilution.
Stain cells for 12 min at room temperature in the dark.
Wash cells once with PBS.
Fix lentiviral-transduced cells in 1% formaldehyde in PBS and incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash cells once with PBS.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer.
Analyze cells for CAR expression using a flow cytometer.
Calculate titer using the equation: Titer (TU/mL) = (F × Cn/V) × DF, where F is % of hEGFRt positive cells/100, Cn is number of cells, V is volume of supernatant in mL, and DF is dilution fold.
Choose dilutions yielding 1%–10% hEGFRt positives for titer calculations.
Isolate T cells from PBMCs using the EasySep™ Human T Cell Enrichment Kit.
Thaw isolated T cells and seed 1 × 10^6 cells per well in a 24-well cell culture plate.
Seed cells in 1 mL AIM-V CST complete medium supplemented with 40 IU/mL human IL-2.
Wash Dynabeads human T-activator CD3/CD28 once with PBS.
Resuspend beads in complete medium and add to T cells at a bead-to-cell ratio of 2:1.
Activate cells for 24 hours before transduction.
Add protamine sulfate into each well to maintain a final concentration of 10 μg/mL.
Replenish the medium with 100 IU/mL of IL-2.
Calculate the volume of CAR-expressing lentivirus using the formula: Multiplicity of Infection (MOI) = Titer (TU/mL) × Volume (mL) / Cell Number.
Add CAR-expressing lentivirus into activated T cells at an MOI of 5.
Centrifuge the cells at 1000 x g for 120 minutes.
Maintain the culture in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 24 hours (Day 2).
Repeat transduction process after another 24 hours (Day 3).
Collect T cells in a 15 mL conical tube on Day 4.
Remove Dynabeads from the collected T cells using a DynaMag magnet.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend CAR T cells in complete T cell medium supplemented with 100 IU/mL of IL-2.
Incubate resuspended CAR T cells at a density of 0.5 × 10^6 cells/mL in a 6-well cell culture plate.
Assess CAR T cell growth every other day by adding fresh medium and IL-2 as needed.
Expand CAR T cells into a T75 flask from Day 6 to Day 7, expecting 10 to 50-fold expansion at the end of the culture period.
Resuspend 1 × 10^6 T cells in FACS buffer containing 1 μg/mL human GPC2-Fc protein or 1 μg/mL anti-EGFR antibody cetuximab for staining.
Incubate the stained cells for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the stained cells once with PBS.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer containing RPE F(ab')2 goat anti-human IgG antibody (1:200 dilution) to detect GPC2-Fc binding or hEGFRt expression.
Add other fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies to mark CD3, CD8, and CD4 for analysis.
Incubate samples for 12 min at room temperature in the dark.
Wash cells once after incubation.
Add DAPI immediately before analysis to stain dead cells.
Draw live cell gate on flow cytometer data.
Draw CD3+ T cell gate from live cell population.
Plot a histogram for CAR expression among transduced cells.
Assess CAR T cell growth until the expected number of cells is reached.
Randomize tumor-bearing mice into different groups based on bioluminescence signals when they exceed the enrollment threshold.
Use bioluminescence signal as baseline measurement for tumor growth monitoring.
Count mock and CAR T cells.
Inject each mouse with 5–10 × 10^6 CAR T cells.
Adjust total T cell number to include respective CAR T cell number.
Calculate corresponding number of mock T cells for control animals based on transduction efficiency.
Resuspend T cells in a volume sufficient for 0.2 mL injection per mouse.
Inject resuspended T cells into mice via tail vein.
Monitor mice bi-weekly for signs of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD).
Track tumor growth longitudinally with weekly bioluminescence imaging.
Obtain weekly weights as part of clinical assessment.
Euthanize the animals at the end of the experiments.
Dissect tumors, spleen, and femurs from euthanized animals.
Weigh and photograph the tumors.
Conduct flow cytometry to assess T cell persistence in various organs.
Retrieve T cells from mouse tissues for functional analysis.
Evaluate tumors for histologic appearance and topographic distribution of T cells.
Cut spleen and tumor tissues into three pieces.
Fix one piece in 4% paraformaldehyde for immunohistochemistry analysis.
Snap-freeze one piece for downstream genomic or proteomic applications.
Dissociate the last piece into a single cell suspension for T-cell isolation via fluorescence-activated cell sorting or magnetic bead isolation.
Fix one femur in 4% paraformaldehyde.
Flush the other femur with PBS.
Count the produced cells and use them for flow cytometry applications.
Use 1 × 10^6 cells per flow cytometric test for analysis.
Analyze the cells isolated from tumor, spleen, and bone marrow by flow cytometry for residual human mock or CAR T-cells.
Quantify GPC2-targeting CAR T-cells using anti-CD3, CD8, CD4, and GPC2-hFc detected by an anti-human Fc antibody.
Count the cells isolated from tumor and normalize to the number of tumor cells and weight.
Quantify the antigen persistence in isolated tumor cells using CT3 antibody and a secondary anti-mouse antibody.
Homogenize frozen tissues using the Bullet Blender tissue homogenizer.
Extract RNA, protein, and genomic DNA from homogenized tissues.
Use extracted RNA and protein for analysis of gene enrichment and identification of CAR interaction partners.
Use genomic DNA to analyze CAR integration sites and quantify CAR copy numbers in tissues.
Perform immunohistochemistry analysis on paraffin-embedded tumor sections from step 24 for T cell markers such as CD3.
